title: Audit-aware analytics role hierarchy and field-level masking
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce an audit-aware RBAC layer for analytics endpoints and usage views that enforces a role hierarchy and supports field-level masking and query auditing. This ticket scopes the backend changes to: (1) a canonical role-to-analytics-permission mapping; (2) enforcement at the query gateway for all analytics endpoints (REST and internal stream consumers); (3) field-level masking rules for PII and billing-sensitive columns; (4) query audit logs that capture redaction decisions and policy hits for compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: API: Console analytics endpoints return only authorized columns according to role and workspace scope
Audit: Every analytics read/write returns a structured audit entry (user, role, route, resource, columns_masked, policy_version)
Performance: End-to-end 95th percentile latency for common usage queries increases by no more than 10% in staging
Compatibility: Existing dashboards and ad-hoc exports continue to work for admin roles without masking
Tests: Unit and integration tests covering policy matrix, masking, and fallback behavior exist and run in CI
technical_notes: Enforcement model: two-tier — gateway filter (service-side ACLs) + DB row-level policies for sensitive datasets
DB approach: use Postgres RLS and view-based materialized aggregates for heavy queries; materialized views have column-level permissions and masked columns where necessary
Masking rules: configurable per-column policies: full-hide, partial-mask (hash/obfuscate), pseudonymize; policy evaluated with deterministic salt per-org for reproducible masking
Policy store: keep canonical policy definitions in service config (YAML) with versioning; store applied policy_version in audit records
Audit store: structured events written to internal eventbus (kafka) then persisted to long-term audit table (immutable) with retention policy and export hooks
Gateway: console-analytics-gateway will attach effective permissions to query context and short-circuit unauthorized column access; will call policy evaluator library maintained in this repo
Backfill: run a one-off job to annotate existing dashboards with their required permission set to avoid surprise breakage for admin users
Fallback: for unsupported queries, return 403 for insufficient privileges or fallback to admin-derived aggregated view for read-only low-cardinality metrics
Performance considerations: avoid per-row function calls for masking in hot paths; prefer pre-materialized masked columns for high-volume metrics
Ops: include rollout plan with canary on internal tenants followed by staged rollout to production backbone regions
decisions: Adopt two-tier enforcement (gateway + DB RLS) to balance defense-in-depth and low-latency queries
Implement masking at column level with three modes (hide, mask, pseudonymize) instead of ad-hoc SQL transformations
Audit events will contain policy_version and a masked_columns array to make compliance audits deterministic
Keep canonical policies in repo as YAML and expose via Console UI for audit but not runtime editing (runtime config via feature flags)
Do not introduce a new external authorization service for this phase; use existing entitlement syncer and local policy evaluator to reduce scope
